# Every control flow action is varied, not just if.
#
# TestPage renders with two items and an empty footer. It catches emptying
# the range, emptying what the range prints, and dropping the {{template}}
# call, because all three change the string it compares.
#
# It never renders with a footer, so the {{with}} body never runs. Emptying
# the {{with}} pipeline and emptying the action inside its body both leave
# the output the test sees untouched, and both survive.
#
# The range declares two variables. A range cannot be emptied by replacing
# its pipeline with 0 in that form -- text/template refuses to iterate over
# an integer with more than one variable -- so the whole construct is
# replaced by its else branch instead.

muxt test-template-mutations -v --seed 1
cmp stdout want.txt

-- go.mod --
module server

go 1.24
-- templates.gohtml --
{{define "page"}}<ul>{{range $i, $item := .Items}}<li>{{$item}}</li>{{end}}</ul>{{with .Footer}}<p>{{.}}</p>{{end}}{{template "brand"}}{{end}}
{{define "brand"}}<b>muxt</b>{{end}}
-- template.go --
package server

import (
	"embed"
	"html/template"
	"io"
)

//go:embed *.gohtml
var templateFiles embed.FS

var templates = template.Must(template.ParseFS(templateFiles, "*.gohtml"))

type Page struct {
	Items  []string
	Footer string
}

func Render(w io.Writer, page Page) error {
	return templates.ExecuteTemplate(w, "page", page)
}
-- render_test.go --
package server

import (
	"strings"
	"testing"
)

func TestPage(t *testing.T) {
	var buf strings.Builder
	if err := Render(&buf, Page{Items: []string{"a", "b"}}); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if got, want := buf.String(), "<ul><li>a</li><li>b</li></ul><b>muxt</b>"; got != want {
		t.Errorf("page = %q, want %q", got, want)
	}
}
